root.name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Charousek Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Be7

overview: Black delays ...Nf6 with 3...Be7, avoiding the Bg5 pin and keeping options. After 4.Nf3 Nf6 White usually reaches a normal QGD, while 4.cxd5 exd5 5.Bf4 gives an Exchange structure with a ...c6 and ...Bd6 set-up for Black. White plays the minority attack or central play, Black the solid structure and ...c5 or ...Bf5.

white_ideas.idea: Transpose to a normal QGD with Nf3 and Bg5 or Bf4.
In the Exchange, play the minority attack with b4-b5.

black_ideas.idea: Hold d5 with ...e6 and free the c8 bishop with ...c6 and ...Bf5.

typical_structures.structure: Carlsbad structure after cxd5 exd5, White minority attack against ...c6/...d5.

character.notes: Slow and technical with a strong reputation for soundness.

gambit.notes: No material is given; the QGD is not a real gambit.

structure.notes: A QGD centre with the tension between c4 and d5 unresolved.

approach.notes: A respected, less common move order choice.

sublines_that_differ.name: Alatortsev Exchange
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 e6 3. Nc3 Be7 4. cxd5 exd5 5. Bf4
sublines_that_differ.how: An Exchange structure with Black playing ...c6 and ...Bd6.

character.reason: A sturdy QGD pawn structure with slow, technical play.

structure.reason: The centre stays in tension in the QGD set-up.

level.reason: Needs structural understanding but little memorisation.

plans.reason: The Exchange branch leads to the classic minority attack.
